title: Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Respect elders' knowledge. Herbal medicine is discussed as knowledge, never as advice to take any remedy.

skills.key_step: The child names types of indigenous knowledge, what they were used for, and how they can be used with modern knowledge.

floor.question: Name one method of traditional education.

representations: a proverb and a weather sign
steps: Say how it was passed on.
Say what it was used for.
Say how it can be used with modern knowledge.

board.do: Write a proverb such as "Unity is strength".

misconceptions.ask: How was indigenous knowledge mainly passed on?
misconceptions.repair: Ask an elder to explain a proverb or a weather sign and note that it was never written.

misconceptions.ask: Which is an indigenous knowledge system?
misconceptions.repair: Sort examples: from elders long ago (herbal medicine, weather signs) or modern.

misconceptions.ask: What was indigenous knowledge used for?
misconceptions.repair: Name a use for each: weather signs for planting, herbs for healing, proverbs for values.

misconceptions.ask: A farmer listens to the radio forecast and also watches for signs elders taught. Is this wise?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a forecast with a traditional sign for the same season.

checks.question: Name two indigenous knowledge systems.
checks.answer: any two of: oral literature, herbal medicine, weather forecasting, farming skills, crafts
